entries.definition: The angle of the Sun's centre above the local horizontal plane.
entries.formula: elevation = angle(Sun direction, local horizontal)
entries.impact: It shows how high the Sun is above the local horizon.
entries.uncertainty: Terrain timing uncertainty is reported separately through clearance and event bounds.

entries.definition: Clearance is the Sun-centre elevation relative to the effective horizon; disk fraction is the visible fraction of the solar disk.
entries.formula: C = el - m_eff(az); disk fraction from chord quadrature
entries.impact: It shows how far above a ridge the Sun is and how much of its disk is visible.
entries.uncertainty: Mask uncertainty affects both clearance and the timing of disk-fraction events.

entries.definition: The apparent oscillation of the Moon's orientation that moves the sub-Earth point in lunar latitude and longitude.
entries.formula: sub-Earth point oscillation, approximately +/-6.7 deg latitude and +/-7.9 deg longitude
entries.impact: It changes Earth direction at a site and can produce Earth rises and sets near the pole.
entries.uncertainty: Computed from the selected lunar ephemeris and frame; it is not a terrain uncertainty.

entries.definition: The reduction in a panel's received solar flux when its normal is not aligned with the Sun direction.
entries.formula: cos(i) = n_panel dot s_hat; upright panel = cos(el) cos(az - heading); loss = 1 - cos(i)
entries.impact: A vertical array produces less power when it faces away from the Sun.
entries.uncertainty: This generic model uses configured panel geometry and efficiency; it is not vehicle-specific performance data.

entries.definition: The Earth-centre elevation above the effective horizon at Earth's azimuth.
entries.formula: DTE margin = Earth elevation - m_eff(Earth azimuth)
entries.impact: It measures how much terrain-clear sky is available in the Earth direction.
entries.uncertainty: Terrain-mask uncertainty affects the horizon term and Earth-event timing.

entries.definition: Geometric visibility of the Moon from a DSN complex when the Moon elevation meets that complex's configured mask.
entries.formula: Moon elevation at Goldstone, Canberra, or Madrid >= configured mask
entries.impact: A ground station must be geometrically able to see the Moon to receive a link.
entries.uncertainty: This is geometric visibility only; it is not a link budget, data-rate, or signal-margin calculation.

entries.definition: Range is the topocentric Earth-to-site distance; one-way light time is that range divided by the speed of light.
entries.formula: range = norm(Earth - site); light time = range / c
entries.impact: It gives the distance and signal travel time between the site and Earth.
entries.uncertainty: The result follows the selected apparent ephemeris geometry; it does not represent communications-system delay.

entries.definition: A label for the terrain-data fidelity available at a site: curated terrain, regional snapped terrain, or smooth-Moon geometry without terrain.
entries.formula: Tier A/B/C as defined by the terrain coverage and evaluator path
entries.impact: It indicates how strongly terrain timing and horizon conclusions can be relied upon.
entries.uncertainty: Tier C has no terrain-mask uncertainty; its times are labelled as smooth-sphere estimates with terrain unavailable, not as terrain-bounded predictions.

entries.definition: A timing half-width derived from horizon-mask uncertainty, or from re-solving the event on shifted masks when available.
entries.formula: fast: delta t = sigma_m(az_event) / abs(dC/dt); exact: half-spread of mask - sigma, nominal, and mask + sigma event times
entries.impact: It shows how far an event time may move when the local horizon is uncertain.
entries.uncertainty: Mask errors are treated as fully correlated in azimuth for shifted-mask passes; no sigma value is implied by this definition.

entries.definition: An event where the body skims the effective horizon and its timing is poorly constrained.
entries.formula: grazing when abs(dC/dt) < 0.005 deg/h, delta t > 12 h, or an event disappears in a shifted-mask pass
entries.impact: A single timestamp is less useful than the reported timing range.
entries.uncertainty: The grazing status is itself an uncertainty warning, not an additional sigma value.

entries.definition: The next transition to a visible Sun disk after the Sun has been blocked by the effective horizon.
entries.formula: next time Sun disk fraction >= configured Sun threshold after a blocked state
entries.impact: It marks when direct sunlight becomes available again under the selected definition.
entries.uncertainty: Its time carries terrain-mask uncertainty when terrain sigma is available.

entries.definition: The longest continuous interval in which generated power is below the mission-profile minimum.
entries.formula: maximum duration of a run with power below the profile minimum
entries.impact: It is the longest interval the battery must support under the selected profile.
entries.uncertainty: Terrain and power-model inputs can change the interval; no battery endurance value is implied.

entries.definition: Time for which generated power is positive and the selected link condition is available.
entries.formula: power-positive AND link
entries.impact: It identifies periods when power and communications are available together.
entries.uncertainty: It inherits the uncertainty and availability assumptions of the power and link inputs.

entries.definition: At polar sites, azimuth measured in the site tangent frame from the projected +X_MOON_ME reference axis rather than from singular geographic north.
entries.formula: azimuth = atan2(dot(v, e), dot(v, n_ref)); n_ref = normalize(a - (a dot u)u), a = +X_MOON_ME at abs(latitude) >= 60 deg
entries.impact: It provides a stable direction convention where geographic north is not unique.
entries.uncertainty: This is a coordinate convention, not an angular-accuracy claim.

entries.definition: Slope is the angle between the fitted ground normal and local up; uphill azimuth is the direction of steepest ascent.
entries.formula: slope = angle(g, u); uphill_az = (downhill_aspect + 180 deg) mod 360 deg
entries.impact: They describe how steep the local pad is and how its orientation can affect panels and nearby occlusion.
entries.uncertainty: Values depend on the fitted DEM plane and its stated fit baseline.

entries.definition: The fitted local plane is used only inside the DEM raycast start distance to model nearby rising ground.
entries.formula: N(az) = atan(tan(theta) cos(az - uphill_az) - h / d_min); N_plus = max(0, N); m_eff = max(m_dem, N_plus) only when N_plus > 0
entries.impact: Nearby uphill ground can hide a low Sun without changing negative or downhill DEM horizons.
entries.uncertainty: It uses the fitted pad plane and d_min metadata; it is not affected by off-nominal lander tilt.

entries.definition: The observer or panel height above the local ground reference used when evaluating the horizon.
entries.formula: spherical-horizon dip is approximately sqrt(2h / R)
entries.impact: Raising the observer can expose more low-elevation sky.
entries.uncertainty: The result remains limited by terrain-mask resolution and local terrain modelling.

entries.definition: Ground distance to the nearest qualifying permanently shadowed region, a cold trap that may host ice.
entries.formula: distance to nearest qualifying PSR boundary
entries.impact: It provides geographic context between a site and nearby permanent shadow.
entries.uncertainty: The value depends on whether the PSR source is published or derived and on the qualifying-region definition.

entries.definition: An educational terrestrial solar-path comparison for an Earth location at the same latitude as the lunar site.
entries.formula: terrestrial solar position at matching latitude over one local solar day
entries.impact: It contrasts lunar illumination with an Earth day at the same latitude.
entries.uncertainty: It is labelled as an educational approximation and is not lunar ephemeris geometry.

entries.definition: A profile-based summary that combines selected criteria and reports GO, MARGINAL, or NO-GO conservatively.
entries.formula: Viability Index = weighted profile components; verdict uses conservative bounds for hard requirements
entries.impact: It summarizes whether the selected scenario meets the stated mission profile.
entries.uncertainty: A GO requires conservative bounds; nominal-only results are provisional or marginal as specified by the evaluator.

entries.definition: The DE421-consistent mean-Earth lunar body-fixed frame used for site coordinates and terrain products.
entries.formula: body-fixed lunar reference frame
entries.impact: It keeps site, terrain, and ephemeris geometry in one stated lunar frame.
entries.uncertainty: Frame selection is a provenance requirement, not a terrain-sigma value.

entries.definition: Azimuth referenced to geographic north where that direction is defined away from the lunar poles.
entries.formula: conversion from the site tangent-frame azimuth to true north where defined
entries.impact: It supports conventional directional interpretation away from the polar singularity.
entries.uncertainty: True north is not used as the polar reference convention.

entries.definition: Lunar longitude increases eastward in the stated MOON_ME coordinate convention.
entries.formula: longitude measured positive east
entries.impact: It fixes the sign convention for site coordinates and map interpretation.
entries.uncertainty: This is a coordinate convention, not a positional-accuracy claim.
